graphic_verification.resolution_of_fuls_W032_conflict: CISI 2 photographs resolve both faces sharply. Face B clearly has three full-height long strokes (W033) beside W700 and W900, while Face A clearly has two full-height long strokes (W032) and two shorter strokes (W002) flanking W840. Fuls's prose coefficient '3' on the W700/W900 face is graphically confirmed on H-904 B; his prose label 'W032' for those three long strokes is a typographical slip for W033.

Q_0011_H904_ICIT3786.missing_witness_to_close_historical_id: Fuls (2020/2023) Figure 16 pixels or authenticated ICIT database crosswalk (HTTP 401).
Q_0011_H904_ICIT3786.implication_for_F0006: Confirms that the physical stroke counts (3 long on B; 2 long and 2 short on A) exist on a real two-face white steatite tablet from Harappa (H-904), eliminating the two-stroke sensitivity branch for H-904. Does NOT establish Fuls's semantic equation 3L + v = 2L + 2S: four additional signs (740 on A; 817-368-645 on B) are omitted from the equation, and no archaeological evidence demonstrates equal quantities or commensurate units across the two faces.

vidale_1987_interim2.source: Vidale 1987, 'More Evidence on a Protohistoric Ceramic Puzzle', Interim Reports Vol. 2, pp. 105-111
vidale_1987_interim2.finding: Describes a fused 1984/1985 DK-B,C kiln-slag block (2 bangles directly observed in 1 inner bowl; conjectural 5 bowls x 2 = 10 bangles, plus 7-bowl anomaly). No mention of M-1383, MN 82a, 82 fragments, or 15-20 bangles.

vidale_1990_ceramics_civilization.source: Vidale 1990, 'Stoneware Industry of the Indus Civilization', Ceramics and Civilization Vol. V, PDF pp. 9-10, Fig. 7
vidale_1990_ceramics_civilization.finding: Reconstructs outer stoneware saggars containing 5-6 inner sub-cylindrical saggars each holding 2-3 bangles (= 10-18 bangles per outer saggar), sealed around the mouth with three oval unicorn-stamped clay sealings before firing. No mention of 82 fragments or a 15-20 count for MN 82a / M-1383.

mackay_1938_vol1.finding: Zero references to MN 82a or stoneware bangle saggars (MN 82a was recovered in 1982, 44 years after Mackay 1938).

Q_0012_M1383_Bangle_Anchor.metadata_conflict_resolution: CISI 2 plate p. 182 completely resolves the prior Lipi 'TAG:R (clay tag)' vs. 'bangle firing pot' conflict: M-1383 A (1) at 15% scale physically depicts the closed cylindrical ceramic saggar, and M-1383 A (2) depicts the unicorn clay sealing applied directly onto its luted mouth. Lipi's 'TAG:R' classifies the impressed clay sealing on the saggar mouth. Visual inspection of M-1383 A (2) also confirms clear 740-575-017-031 on the intact left side and a diagonal crack/erosion across the first three reading-order signs (920-060-741) on the right.

algebraic_sensitivity.critical_note: Under Fuls's unverified 15-20 bangle bound (8 <= L <= 13), only (L, S, v) = (10, 8, 6) survives. Under Vidale (1990)'s published technological range of 10-18 bangles per outer saggar (3 <= L <= 11), THREE of the four exact solutions survive: (4, 20, 36) giving 11, (6, 8, 10) giving 13, and (10, 8, 6) giving 17.

Q_0012_M1383_Bangle_Anchor.implication_for_F0006: Even though M-1383 is confirmed to be a stoneware-bangle saggar sealing, the 82-fragment / 15-20 bangle count remains unverified in all held primary sources, Vidale's published saggar capacity (10-18) fails to isolate L=10 uniquely, and Vidale (1990) reports three oval impressions of a standard unicorn stamp seal per saggar mouth—undermining the premise that a reusable unicorn stamp seal's text encodes the exact bangle count of one firing batch.
